what: a new Facts method (object_trait_lifetimes, for the Unsize to `&dyn Tr` rule) was answered in BorrowFacts but never reached the lowering: every body is lowered through NestedFacts, which forwards each method by hand, and a method it does not forward silently takes the trait's default `None` (not known), so the fix looked inert with no error
cost: one test round and a reading of the facts dump to see the method was never asked
cause: Facts has defaulted methods returning `None`, so a wrapper that forgets one compiles and quietly answers 'not known'
whys: the defaults exist so tests' small Facts impls need not write every method; the same defaults let a forwarding wrapper drop a method
class: any forwarding impl of a trait with defaulted methods (NestedFacts over BorrowFacts, any future wrapper)
prevention: wanted: no defaults on Facts (each impl names every answer), or a lint that a forwarding impl overrides every defaulted method; done for now: NestedFacts forwards object_trait_lifetimes
annoyance: the runner keeps 30 lines of a failure, so a test printing flows must join them into long lines; a typeck panic ('node 6 is not a type', blaze-typeck infer/mod.rs:154) from `fn f<'a>(c: &'a mut Chan) -> impl Future<Output = Option<u8>> + 'static { c.pop() }` (with `async fn pop(&mut self)`) aborts the whole test instead of failing one body
workaround: the test joins each wrong body's flow into lines of at most 1100 bytes; the panicking control was left out of front2_borrows_tempo
